newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-NYMEX crude expires higher, but down on week.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-NYMEX crude expires higher, but down on week.

text.p: NYMEX oil futures erased most of their early losses, with crude and heating oil settling higher but gasoline again lagged the rest of the oil complex and settled lower, traders said.

"The longer the market sat on its side and didn't probe the downside, the more likely it was going to test the upside," said Tom Bentz, analyst at ING Derivatives, noting the fact gasoline ended lower was just "more of the same."
October crude expired nine cents higher at $23.63 a barrel after slipping to a low $23.26 in afternoon trade, but well above last Friday's settlement of $24.51 a barrel.
Heating oil continued to get support from views stocks could be too low ahead of the winter, with the October contract settling 0.65 cent higher at 67.42 cents a gallon.
"The heating oil market is setting itself up to be extremely sensitive to every five-day weather report," said Thomas Blakeslee, analyst at Cargill Investor Services.
But gasoline lagged the complex, burdened by views the imminent arrival of numerous cargoes will weigh heavily on a market characterized by flagging end-of-summer demand.
October gasoline, shaking off an early upside move, settled 0.23 cent lower at 61.09 cents a gallon.
Firm heat and weak gasoline markets are likely to continue next week, helping crude stay in a range, traders said.
That's been the ongoing story for a while," Blakeslee said, referring to the split outlook for heat and gasoline in U.S. energy markets.
He saw November crude, which becomes the nearby contract with the start of ACCESS trade on Sunday evening, to move in a range with resistance at $23.65 a barrel and support at $22.20 a barrel.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
